title: 综合实战：一次低端机卡顿和误杀进程的完整排查
key_conclusions: Low-end memory incidents need one timestamp-aligned timeline that joins frames, bucket growth, reclaim, PSI, ZRAM, lmkd, and adj.
A high-priority kill claim is not proven without kill-time oom_score_adj, process state, RSS, and lmkd evidence.
Bitmap decode and Graphics/Native peaks can be the upstream pressure source behind both jank and lmkd kills.
Watermark, ZRAM, cache, and adj changes should be tested one at a time with explicit rollback lines.
shallow_points: The case is a teaching reconstruction and does not include a real attached Perfetto trace.
The article does not include raw lmkd/statsd protobuf output or exact vendor ROM policy source.
It does not quantify thresholds for PSI, ZRAM swapin, or kill benefit by RAM class.
It does not provide an executable replay script for the image-heavy scroll workload.
discovered_connections: Day 77's timestamp-aligned evidence commands become the collection package for a full incident.

Day 65's high-priority kill taxonomy and Day 64's timing discipline combine into the mistaken-kill branch.
Day 79 should turn this case workflow into a review checklist for launch, canary, and incident response.
suggest_future_topics: Day 79 should focus on an Android memory review checklist for pre-launch, canary, and post-incident stages.

knowledge_gaps: Need real low-end traces with frame timeline, memory PSI, vmstat, zram, and lmkd logs.
Need branch-specific lmkd and OomAdjuster field validation for the target Android version.
Need measured thresholds for acceptable PSI full, swapin, and kill benefit.
Need automated replay tooling to reproduce the case without manual timing drift.
